full_judgment: 23. In the instant suit summons of the previous suit i.e. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was duly served and the defendant entered appearance, but he having not been present on the date when the suit, Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, was taken up for final hearing the same was decreed ex parte. So, it is seen that the ex parte decree which sought to be set aside by initiating new action i.e. by filing Title Suit No. 22 of 1987, fraud alleged as to suppression of summons is not correct. It is seen from the judgment of the trial Court as well as the appellate Court that although the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 i. e. the appellants herein, filed the suit alleging suppression of summons in obtaining the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 but at the time of trial the plaintiff proceeded with the allegation that the claim of the plaintiff of the previous suit as regard the land in suit was false and that the ex parte decree was obtained by perjured evidence. As stated herein before, the trial Court dismissed the suit since allegation of suppression of the summons in obtaining ex parte decree sought to be set aside by initiating new action was not established. The appellate Court upon introducing irrelevant matters totally unconnected with the issue in the suit and that on the basis of baseless presumption as well as upon making aspersions on the Government functionaries resorting to unfounded inference and lastly, to the learned Judge who passed the ex parte decree and also taking the view that the documents relied upon by the plaintiff of the previous suit i.e. defendants in the instant suit, were not genuine, set aside the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit. The High Court Division and in the background of the facts and circumstances of the case of the plaintiff-appellants and the proposition of law laid down as to the ground upon which an ex parte decree can be set aside in a new action filed alleging fraud, arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs failed to establish that there was suppression of summons and thereby they were prevented from placing their case before the Court or that the Court was misled as to the matter of service of summons on the defendant of the previous suit.
